summary: Evening burst: elevated 503s caused by prefetch throttling and runtime restarts
description: Issue summary: Between ~18:30 and 19:10 UTC customers experienced a sharp increase in 503 responses from the hosted API that correlated with a customer traffic burst. Impact: ~12% error rate for Lexicon Labs traffic during the window; streaming sessions dropped and several long-running generation requests failed. Environment: prod-us-east (dedicated pool rwd-ded-14), API gateway cluster agw-07, runtime pool rt-pool-3. Timeline/high level: 1) 18:28 UTC - spike in incoming requests from Lexicon Labs noted by customer. 2) 18:30 UTC - api-gateway 503 counts surge; Datadog alarm triggered. 3) 18:32 UTC - several runtime pods restarted with OOM messages in kernel logs. 4) 18:35-19:05 UTC - sustained elevated 503s, streaming disconnects reported. 5) 19:08 UTC - temporary mitigation (increased autoscaler burst) applied and errors dropped. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send concurrent streaming generation requests (50-80 parallel sessions) with long prefix contexts and frequent small deltas to simulate Lexicon traffic pattern. 2) Observe api-gateway 503 rate and runtime memory usage. Observed artifacts and links: - Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/sup/rg-agw-503s (api-gateway 5xx panel) - Datadog traces: https://app.datadoghq.com/trace/trace-search?query=SUP-90021 - Runtime logs (pod rt-xyz): /var/log/containers/rt-xyz.log and k8s events show OOMKilled entries. Preliminary metrics: - api-gateway 5xx rate +1100% during peak - runtime restarts: 7 restarts across 4 pods - kvcache evictions spiked by 8x - autoscaler did not add new nodes for ~90s due to cooldown Hypothesis: A sudden burst of requests with heavy KV cache misses caused runtime memory pressure and excessive prefetch work. Prefetch throttling combined with blocked worker threads led to downstream proxy timeouts (503) and a cascade of runtime restarts (OOM). Next actions: - Collect full runtime heap profiles and core dumps for affected pods (requested). - Temporarily increase autoscaler burst capacity for rwd-ded-14 and extend cooldown window for burst events. - Adjust prefetch parallelism for affected runtime version to limit memory growth. - Add targeted alerting on kvcache eviction rate and prefetch queue length. Cross-references: see linked_issues and related_prs for patches and follow-ups.

investigation_notes: Reproduction: synthetic load generator reproduced the error pattern when prefetch parallelism >=16 and KV miss rate >60%. Heap profiles collected show memory allocations dominated by prefetch buffers and token cache duplication. Kernel OOM logs indicate container RSS exceeded 95% of pod memory limit. Observed that api-gateway uses a 10s upstream timeout which amplifies 503s when runtimes stall. Hotfix applied: autoscaler burst increased from 2->6 nodes for rwd-ded-14. Temporary mitigation succeeded but root fix requires runtime prefetch throttling + better kvcache metrics.
resolution_notes: Mitigations applied 2026-03-13 19:00-19:10 UTC: 1) Increased autoscaler burst for affected pool to reduce time-to-scale. 2) Adjusted api-gateway upstream retry window to allow short stalls (reduced early 503 amplification). 3) Rolled out canary of prefetch cap (PR #1123) to 10% of traffic; no regressions observed. Customer service: Lexicon Labs informed and ticket updated. Planned follow-ups: - Permanently lower default prefetch parallelism in next runtime release. - Add alerting on kvcache eviction spikes and prefetch queue length. - Update runbook: include guidance for dedicated pools under bursty KV-miss patterns.
